prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1031; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the intersection in Houston, Texas, I found a rear-end collision between two vehicles. Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of Driver 1's car. The impact appeared light, and both vehicles were drivable from the scene. The damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle and the front of Driver 2's vehicle is consistent with the reported impact. Witnesses, photographs taken at the scene, and Driver 2's statement all describe the collision in the same manner. Passenger was in Driver 1's vehicle at the time, and both the witnesses and I confirmed this. Driver 1 reported back strain and described the pain as severe, although the low-force nature of the impact seems insufficient to account for that level of injury. A few older scratches on the rear bumper may predate this collision, and I have not determined their origin. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle.
